title: A proper zero-dimensional scheme over a field is finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $\dim Y\le0$ [def-pc-dimension]. Then the structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $Y$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], and $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space.

proof.text: Because $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, it is of finite type by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Thus $Y$ is an algebraic $k$-scheme in the sense of Tag 06LH.

source.place: Tag 06LH (Varieties, Lemma algebraic-scheme-dim-0), with the definition of proper morphism providing finite type

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] to the finite-type scheme $Y$ and the hypothesis $\dim Y\le0$. It gives that $Y$ is affine and that its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite.

For a finite morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] identifies the source as affine and shows that $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. This supplies the final assertion.
